Registration cache: stock vs patched modules

Pageable copies from THP buffers at the sizes progressive pinning runs (4 MiB, its first chunk, to 1 GiB, the default registration cap), median of every sample (3 processes of 2 each). Progressive pinning is the hook with the default request, audited as cmt tune audits it; on the stock modules the hook cannot pin, and the audited child refused in 6 of 6 processes (path/count mismatch), so there is no stock line unless one completed. pin_pipeline (register 32 MiB ahead of the copy, unpin at the end) runs on both modules: its gain from stock to patched is the patch's, not the algorithm's. The table: pin and unpin rates of the whole buffer, and pin + copy + unpin, at the largest size.

Workloads: stock vs hook

Each dot is one run; the bar is the median; y starts at zero. The number under a name is the hook speedup: stock / hook median when lower is better, hook / stock when higher is better, so above 1 means the hook helped. "!" flags fewer runs than requested or unequal arms; such records are still drawn. A warm-up run of the stock command, when the runner recorded one, is listed but never in a median. The hook arm used tune/full/tune.json. Result: faster when the speedup is at least 1.05× and every hooked run beat every stock run; slower when it is at most 1/1.05× and every hooked run lost to every stock run; otherwise no clear change.
